sources.title: Handbook-first communication
quotes: GitLab is intentional about documenting in a manner that creates a single source of truth.
At GitLab, we write things down *first*, and communicate that (E.g. Document the solution first, *then* announce via Slack or email.).

sources.title: GitLab communication
quotes: To accomplish this, we use asynchronous communication as a starting point and stay as open and transparent as we can by communicating through public issues, merge requests, and Slack channels.
We also place an emphasis on ensuring that conclusions of offline conversations are written down.
We communicate respectfully and professionally at all times.

sources.title: Remote onboarding
quotes: GitLab believes the onboarding process is incredibly important. We don't expect anyone to hit the ground running from day one.

We anticipate the remote onboarding process to take at least two full weeks, with the third week designated for team-specific onboarding and training. We encourage new team members to participate in their teams' work in the first two weeks, but without pressure to contribute heavily.

sources.title: Meeting agendas
quotes: Every work-related meeting should have a single live doc agenda affixed to the calendar invite at the time that the invite is added to calendars.
[Meeting DRIs](/handbook/people-group/directly-responsible-individuals/) should prep the agenda at least 72 hours before the meeting.
